        "statement": "Let a graph property be a partition of the unlabeled graphs on a fixed number of vertices into graphs with and without the property.   "321554": {

    "title": "The maximal-dimension conjecture for 1-spec matrix spaces",
    "literal_statement": "Let $V$ be a $1$-spec subspace of $\\operatorname{M}_n(\\mathbb{K})$ such that\n\n$$\n\\dim V=1+\\binom{n}{2}.\n$$\n\nAssume $n>4$. A linear subspace $W$ of $\\operatorname{M}_n(\\mathbb{K})$ has a **trivial spectrum** if no element of $W$ has a nonzero eigenvalue. **Maximal-dimension conjecture.** There exists a linear subspace $W$ of $\\operatorname{M}_n(\\mathbb{K})$ with a trivial spectrum such that\n\n$$\nV=\\mathbb{K}I_n+W.\n$$\n\nThe conjecture concerns the classification of $1$-spec subspaces of maximal dimension and, if true, would resolve the question for $\\#\\mathbb{K}>2$ and $n>4$ using the cited results on affine spaces of nonsingular matrices.   "321621": {
    "mathdb_id": 321621,
    "title": "The extension-graph conjecture for right-angled Artin groups",
    "literal_statement": "Let $\\Lambda$ and $\\Gamma$ be finite graphs. For a graph $\\Gamma$, its **extension graph** $\\Gamma^e$ has as vertices the elements of $A(\\Gamma)$ conjugate to vertices of $\\Gamma$, with two vertices adjacent exactly when the corresponding elements commute. Write $\\Lambda\\leq\\Gamma^e$ when $\\Lambda$ is an induced subgraph of $\\Gamma^e$.\n\n**Extension-graph conjecture.**\n\n$$\nA(\\Lambda)\\leq A(\\Gamma)\\quad\\text{if and only if}\\quad\\Lambda\\leq\\Gamma^e.\n$$\n\nThe forward implication is conjectured because every known embedding has arisen from an inclusion into an extension graph; the reverse implication is established by the paper's first main theorem.     "title": "The two-dimensional sumset lower-bound conjecture for valid multisets",
    "literal_statement": "Let $p$ be a prime and let $A$ be a **valid multiset** contained in $\\mathbb{Z}_p^2$: it contains no zero element, and every nontrivial subgroup contains fewer than $p$ elements of $A$, counted with multiplicity.   "322716": {
    "mathdb_id": 322716,
    "title": "Nonnegative coefficient conjecture for three-residue partition products",
    "literal_statement": "Let $L>0$, $z>1$, $y>z$, $y<x\\leq y+z$, and $m\\geq yz+2$. For the finite $q$-Pochhammer symbol $(a;q^m)_L=\\prod_{j=0}^{L-1}(1-aq^{mj})$, define\n\n$$\n\\frac{1}{(q,q^{x},q^{yz};q^{m})_L}-\\frac{1}{(q^z,q^{y},q^{yz+1};q^{m})_L}=\\sum_{n=1}^{\\infty}a(L,y,n,x,z,m)q^n.\n$$\n\n**Three-residue coefficient conjecture.** If $z$ does not divide $y$, then all coefficients $a(L,y,n,x,z,m)$ are non-negative; if $z$ divides $y$, then only finitely many of these coefficients are negative.\n\nThis conjecture extends the paper's partition inequalities to three residues and distinguishes the cases according to whether $z$ divides $y$.     "title": "Hansen's Szeged–Wiener index conjecture for bipartite graphs",
    "literal_statement": "Let $G$ be a finite, simple, connected bipartite graph with $n \\geq 4$ vertices and $m \\geq n$ edges.     "title": "Symmetry conjecture for optimal even small polygons",
    "literal_statement": "Let $n\\geq 6$ be even, and let $A_n^*$ denote the maximal area among all small $n$-gons. An **optimal $n$-gon** is a small $n$-gon whose area is $A_n^*$. Its diameter graph is the graph whose vertices are the polygon's vertices, with edges joining pairs at distance equal to the diameter, and a **pendant edge** is an edge incident to a vertex of degree one. **Symmetry conjecture.** For even $n\\geq 6$, an optimal $n$-gon has an axis of symmetry corresponding to the pendant edge in its diameter graph.     "literal_statement": "Let $v,w\\in\\mathfrak{S}_n$ with $v\\leq w$, and let $Q_{v,w}$ be the Bruhat interval polytope whose vertices are the permutations $u\\in[v,w]$. Equivalently, if the graphs $\\widetilde{G}^{v,w}_v$ and $\\widetilde{G}^{v,w}_v$ are forests, then $\\widetilde{G}^{v,w}_u$ is a forest for every $v\\leq u\\leq w$. This generalizes Conjecture 7.16 of Le–Ma, which concerns the corresponding case with the lower endpoint equal to the identity permutation.
